newsitem.title: USA: Stocks set new high; Dow trades briefly above 5,900. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Stocks set new high; Dow trades briefly above 5,900. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]

text.p: Blue-chip stocks soared again Monday, sending the Dow Jones industrial average briefly through 5,900 points for the first time just one session after cracking the 5,800 level on hopes that the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates unchanged.
"It's pretty amazing. It's got 6,000 written all over it," said Jim Benning, a trader at BT Brokerage.
"It's more follow-through buying than anything else. Numbers are coming in perfect and there's the belief the Fed won't raise rates," he said.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 50.68 points, or 0.87 percent, at a record 5,889.20 (corrects figure from 5,889.29) after breaching the 5,900 level in late trading for the first time. On Friday, it set a new milestone of 5,838.52.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 3.44 to 683.98, topping Friday's record closing high of 680.54.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks was up 1.72 to 365.42, surpassing its old record close of 363.74 set on May 24.
The Nasdaq Composite gained 5.29 to 1,193.96, still off the all-time high close of 1,249.15 set June 5.
In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines 1,397 to 978 on heavy volume of 430 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Dow soared 178.66 points last week -- its second biggest weekly point gain ever as investors turned upbeat on economic data that pointed to moderating growth and benign inflation.
Last week, the government said the Consumer Price Index inched up just 0.1 percent and the Producer Price Index edged up 0.3 percent in August confirming that inflation was still dormant.
There had been widespread expectations that the Fed was ready to raise interest rates at the first sign of inflation.
Now, Wall Street is betting that the Sept. 24 meeting of the central bank's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee will keep short-term interest rates unchanged.

"It seems increasingly clear the Fed won't do anything," said Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter. "That means earnings are not at risk of a hike in interest rates and opens up a window of opportunity for stocks until the election," he said. "We're heading past 6,000."
Some analysts were mystified by the stock boom, noting that fundmentals, such as moderating corporate earnings growth and a yield near 7 percent on the 30-year Treasury bond, remained worrisome.

Robert Stovall, president of Stovall/21st Advisers, said, "The fundamentals haven't changed much. The markets assume Clinton will be re-elected and there is the record of poor markets for the first year of second-term presidents."
"In the absence of anything, the money is there. People have identified equities -- mainly big equities -- is the place to be," he said.
In the bond market, the yield on the Treasury's 30-year held at Friday's close of 6.95 percent.

Stocks got a boost after Dean Witter raised its stock allocation in its basic asset portfolio to 60 percent from 55 percent, cut cash to 20 percent from 25 percent and left bonds unchanged at 20 percent.

Among individual stocks, U.S. Filter surged 3-7/8 to 30-1/2 and Wheelabrator Technologies added 3/8 to 14-3/4 after U.S. Filter agreed to buy Wheelabrator's industrial water process and manufacturing units for $385 million. The companies also agreed to set up a joint venture.
Glenayre tumbled 40 percent or 13-1/4 to 20. The company warned of an earnings shortfall for the third quarter.
Anadigics, which also warned that its third-quarter results would fall short of analysts' expectations, lost 7-5/8 to 21-7/8.
America Online rose 2 to 29 in its first day of trading on the NYSE, moving from the Nasdaq stock market.
Citizens Bancorp rallied 14-3/4 to 47 and Crestar Financial lost 2-1/4 to 59-1/8 on news of a merger estimated at $774 million.

CheckFree Corp. added 3-3/16 to 21-1/4. Intuit Inc. and CheckFree agreed to a deal in which Intuit will swap Intuit Services Corp., its back-end bill payment processing unit, in exchange for a stake of 23 percent in CheckFree. Intuit rose 2-1/8 to 32-1/4.
Nike class B shares added 2-3/8 to 121-5/8 after it reported a 24 percent jump in quarterly profits and its board approved a two-for-one stock split.
The American Stock Exchange index rose 0.68 of a point to 570.94. The average NYSE share was up 18 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,702.627 up 31.519 or 0.47 percent.
